title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 9): Grifter by day, Porker by night
summary: Part 9 of NH's hostile series on YouTuber Jason Blaha. NH alleges that Blaha posted lies on forums, bought fake subscribers to reach 100k, and uses fake or technical plates to fake strength progress, and he warns a young client against being coached by him. Training points along the way: realistic overhead press progression, competition as the only proof of strength, and accessory PRs as a cope.
claims: NH alleges Blaha signed a very young, tall client with a large following in order to attract more young clients, and that the kid would have made the same noob gains on a 5x5
Novices gain strength on almost any program, so a coach claiming credit for a beginner's noob gains is misleading
NH calls the ectomorph label a myth (ectomorphs do not exist)
A tall teenager deadlifting with a rounded back under bad coaching is headed for injury
Forums are full of pathological liars because nobody can see you; NH moderated forums for a while
Being pitiless with scammers who target the weak is necessary; giving them endless chances is why they keep hurting people
YouTube rewards early starters; once a channel passes 100k subs the algorithm usually pushes it hard, so a channel that stalls there is suspicious
NH alleges Blaha hid his subscriber count while losing subs, bought fake subs to reach 100k, and gets fewer views per video than NH despite ten times the subs
Rogue sells red technical plates that look like 55 lb bumpers but weigh much less; swapping two in fakes roughly 100 lb on the bar
The only way to verify a home-gym lift is to weigh the plates on camera, load them on camera and lift; ideally a sanctioned meet
Liars prepare their audience in advance; insisting your plates are calibrated can be groundwork against future fake-weight accusations
Jumping from a 165 lb overhead press for 3 to 225 lb is not realistic; the overhead press progresses slowest of all lifts, and adding 10 lb can take a long time, 60 lb two to three years
Going from struggling with bodyweight dips to repping +90 lb is not a plausible progression for a lifter with 20 years of training
You do not stop training a lift for six months and come back stronger
Adding 100 lb to chin-ups, dips and overhead press would visibly change your physique; strength jumps without size change are a red flag
A 600 lb squat to depth in competition with real plates, a straight bar and no box is what powerlifting is; box or cambered-bar squats do not count
Constantly blaming weak points like triceps for years without progress shows you do not know how to train; NH says Blaha avoids isolation and high reps
Low range-of-motion good mornings with huge loads will not train the spinal erectors
A 40 lb close-grip bench PR right after an injury is not plausible
Gym equipment loses value once used; it is not an investment like stocks
Claiming PRs on accessory variations, new bars, bands and chains is a cope when the big three have not progressed
The powerlifting community has a lot of delusion and mental illness, and many lolcows are strength-focused
